scope: Point-in-time predictor values from native batch features; successive-prefix inference evaluated separately
finding: Reproduced within-split lookahead in quantile_price_lines: 173 of 192 existing rows changed after extending to 384 rows. Both control configurations changed zero rows. Failed independent probe on quantile_price_lines; no generic causal enforcement.
limitation: Observed count describes this fixture/configuration only; it is not a population defect rate. Split-first processing does not remove this within-split lookahead. Shipped native LightGBM prep includes this feature. This is a failure of historical row values computed over complete evaluation batches. Using only the final row of successive available prefixes can be causal; that distinct path is not invalidated merely by calling the same function.

scope: Built-in MLManifest preparation versus arbitrary Python callbacks
finding: Native path splits raw input first and fits preprocessing on training data. Custom callbacks and a pre-split selector can see broader data; no universal isolation guarantee. Implemented for built-in split-first and fitted preprocessing; caller-dependent for custom functions.
limitation: Pre-split selector sees complete admitted frame; arbitrary feature callables are not inspected for causality; custom architecture gets entire prepared dictionary.

scope: Built-in forward targets and bound private trade labels
finding: Built-in shifted labels are censored within splits; trade labels expose availability. Custom label horizons and availability require explicit verification. Partial: split-local forward-label censoring and explicit trade-label availability; caller-supplied label semantics unverified.
limitation: No universal derivation of generic walk-forward purge from target horizon. Physical split-local generation already prevents these built-in targets from reading next split, so missing auto sizing is not itself demonstrated leakage.

scope: Configured walk-forward and ordinary ratio/date splitters
finding: Walk-forward enforces ordered timestamps, fold geometry and configured purge/embargo. Gaps are not generally derived automatically from target horizons. Implemented explicit walk-forward geometry; stronger validation than default positional splitter.
limitation: Walk-forward requires sorted unique datetimes but does not enforce a universal regular cadence; raw row-count gaps are not automatically label/event-time gaps. Generic ratio split slices current row order.

finding: Walk-forward refits copied manifests per fold. Conditional stacking uses earlier completed labels and refits its scaler/PCA inside inner folds. Implemented locally with explicit availability purge.
limitation: The underlying feature functions have already been applied to raw training rows; noncausal features remain possible. This is not a universal nested-validation protocol.

scope: Built-in binary model calibration and event validation objective
finding: Native calibration and threshold selection use validation data. Using the same validation sample for both is selection, not an independent performance estimate. Validation-only selection implemented; independent calibration assessment remains external.
limitation: Configured validation score is optimized on that same sample, so it is not an unbiased future-performance estimate. Objective currently permits specific binary built-ins and event execution only.

scope: Binary metrics, walk-forward summaries and execution return tapes
finding: Explicit metric implementations exist, but finite fold results are averaged arithmetically. balanced_metric means precision times square root of positive prediction rate. Implemented with materially different conventions requiring normalization.
limitation: Mean fold return is not concatenated compounded return; averaged counts are not pooled confusion counts. Finite-only averaging can hide unavailable fold metrics.

scope: DSR/PBO and numerical correctness test surfaces
finding: DSR/PBO formulas, edge checks and alternate in-repository formula assertions exist. Snapshot execution parity was independently measured. Numerical agreement does not establish inferential calibration or generalization. Implemented formulas and local oracle/property checks; statistical calibration unproven.
limitation: An alternate formula in the same repository is useful verification but not independent academic validation or empirical false-positive calibration.

finding: Convergence warnings and missing evidence are recorded. A warned model can remain successful/selected; diagnostic reporting is not an admission gate. Diagnostic warning frequency implemented; no automatic model exclusion.
limitation: Absence of this warning is not proof of optimization convergence. Default warning evidence does not prevent downstream selection; user warning-as-error settings can abort.

scope: Per-run returns/CSV and explicitly supplied experiment families
finding: Recorded local successes/failures and family identity checks support accounting. Unlogged, deleted, external or pruned search history is not globally recoverable. Partial local inventory; no global complete search history.
limitation: Failed attempts lack return tracks; supplied runs do not reveal deleted, crashed, pruned, external or undisclosed searches. Local count is not effective independent-trial count.

finding: DSR/PBO diagnostics are conditional on retained comparable tracks. Default two-block PBO has only three possible values; no serial-covariance correction in DSR. Implemented conditional diagnostics, with important inferential limits.
limitation: Statistics are not auto acceptance gates: report verdict false/null does not reject training or Sensor creation. No universal correction for adaptive search, regime dependence or hidden trials.

scope: Family acceptance reports over supplied directories
finding: Family diagnostics check aligned timestamps and execution identity and withhold unsupported conclusions. Snapshot joint PBO lacks full comparable source identity. Implemented conservative grouping; snapshot joint PBO withheld.
limitation: Declared source identities are not independently verified; snapshot artifacts lack full OHLC execution identity so family PBO is unavailable; family selection itself can add multiplicity.

scope: Reserved local holdout for native dated binary Sensors/Cohorts
finding: Reserved holdout freezes supported fitted state and records attempts before loading data. Research and final-assessment compatibility is substantially restricted. Strong restricted protocol; incompatible with several principal research modes.
limitation: Only native exact LogRegBinary/LightGBMBinary inference with dated non-event data; reservation refuses custom SFDs, WF, parallel/factorized/resume/profile/bars/event/funding/callbacks. Repeated assessments are labelled, not prohibited; external exposure always unknown.

scope: Fixed strategy baselines, random actions and future use claims
finding: Executable strategy references exist. No external-comparator ranking, profitable generalization or cross-venue robustness was established in this review. Baseline code available; comparative profitable generalization unknown.
limitation: RandomBinary maps random actions to .9/.1 scores and uses global RNG, so it is not a calibrated probabilistic null. Correct implementation tests do not establish market edge.

scope: Feature ablation, recorded evidence and parameter diagnostics
finding: Seeded feature ablation and replay mechanisms exist. IID trial-row correlation bootstrap is not a dependence-aware market-return uncertainty estimate. Partial mechanisms implemented; robustness outcomes require measurement.
limitation: IID trial-row bootstrap intervals describe sampled trial correlations, not time-series strategy-return uncertainty or causal feature importance. Rich artifacts alone do not guarantee stable generalization.

scope: Algorithm time, History API and native return windows
finding: AlgorithmManager sets current algorithm time/slice before scheduled and data callbacks. Native History clamps requests ending after UtcTime. ReturnsSymbolData maintains a bounded rolling window of updates and admits ROC observations only once ready.
limitation: These are concrete native information-set protections. They do not prove point-in-time correctness of arbitrary custom data, external reads, training callbacks or every indicator/model; provider timestamp/normalization semantics still matter.

scope: Native online portfolio estimation versus general ML
finding: Mean-variance portfolio construction warms bounded return state from current History and optimizes that local return matrix; algorithm Train schedules caller-supplied training code.
limitation: This provides native online estimation boundaries, not an enforced supervised training/evaluation split. Train does not inspect feature fitting, targets or test reuse; full ML research isolation requires an adapter.

finding: Native Train forwards an action to the scheduler; the inspected portfolio path consumes current insight magnitudes and bounded returns.
limitation: A general label horizon/censoring protocol was not located in these native scheduling/portfolio APIs. Custom supervised models need an adapter with explicit outcome-availability timestamps.

scope: Online history length and training schedules
finding: ReturnsSymbolData has explicit ROC lookback and window period; Train can schedule updates on configured date/time rules.
limitation: These are online-window controls, not purged/embargoed/nested validation. Native parameter optimization enumerates configurations without automatically constructing a disjoint final research holdout.

scope: Native return matrix and portfolio fitting boundary
finding: Portfolio construction creates a return matrix from bounded symbol state and passes it to the selected optimizer, which derives covariance/expected returns if not supplied.
limitation: General fold-fitted transforms and OOF stacking are not owned by this interface. Insight magnitudes and custom optimizers remain supplied code; historical-moment fitting does not establish nested supervised validation.

finding: The generic Train API schedules arbitrary training actions and the optimizer can target user-chosen statistics.
limitation: A built-in supervised probability-calibration/threshold-nesting protocol was not located in these APIs. Such behavior can be implemented by users but requires a separately audited adapter.

finding: Portfolio statistics separately calculate elapsed-time compounded annual return. The AnnualPerformance helper compounds the arithmetic mean daily return, while annual variance multiplies daily variance by tradingDaysPerYear; portfolio Sharpe uses that annual performance and a modeled risk-free rate.
limitation: This native Sharpe numerator is not mean daily excess return times sqrt(periods), nor realized geometric CAGR. Sortino uses variance of below-target returns. Standard-deviation/moment dependency conventions, annualization, risk-free source and zero sentinels must be normalized in a common metric contract.

scope: Inspected numerical and model regression tests
finding: PSR tests cover equal/greater/lower benchmark and risk-free response. Portfolio optimizer tests assert known weight vectors and explicit equal-weight fallback cases.
limitation: Tests were inspected, not executed in this academic audit. Boundary expectations and same-implementation PSR benchmark comparisons do not independently validate moment conventions, statistical assumptions or all fill/accounting paths.

finding: MaximumSharpeRatioPortfolioOptimizer tests positive-excess-return feasibility, inspects solver success and normalizes the solution; infeasibility/solver failure/nonpositive recovery sum falls back to equal weights.
limitation: Fallback is a usable allocation convention, not proof a fitted optimum converged. It is returned as an ordinary weight vector without a distinct downstream convergence record in this interface. General user Train convergence remains caller-owned.

scope: Native optimizer counts and completed metrics
finding: LeanOptimizer tracks completed/failed/running/queued counts and retains parsed per-backtest metrics with parameters/backtest IDs. Grid search processes results only after nonempty JSON arrives.
limitation: Null/invalid result metrics are omitted from completed analysis; counters/logs do not reconstruct every failed artifact or external/manual trial. Post-search analysis explicitly filters to parsed portfolio statistics and selects its summary best by Sharpe, irrespective of the optimization target.

scope: Native probabilistic Sharpe and optional objective constraints
finding: PSR uses observed Sharpe, skewness/kurtosis and sample count against a fixed benchmark; reported portfolio PSR uses annual Sharpe1 deannualized. Optimizer constraints can filter result statistics.
limitation: PSR is not deflated Sharpe: no searched-trial count or family maximum enters this formula, and no serial-covariance correction appears. It is reported evidence, not an automatic protected-research admission rule. Moment conventions inherited from MathNet were not independently verified here.

scope: Saved algorithm results and optimization analysis
finding: Backtest result construction includes chart/order/P&L/statistics/configuration/state outputs; optimization tracks result IDs and parameters before computing parameter/family summaries.
limitation: The inspected output and optimizer paths do not establish equality of all market-input bytes, source/dependency revisions and statistical protocols across independent runs. Common run manifests are still needed; completed-result analysis alone omits null failures.

finding: Native optimizer applies target/constraint selection to returned backtest results, while Train accepts arbitrary user code.
limitation: No native reserved single-use final holdout/freeze-before-access protocol was located in these scheduling/optimizer surfaces. A separate research adapter must distinguish repeated validation from untouched final evidence.

finding: Native portfolio statistics include benchmark beta/alpha/tracking/information ratios and a configurable risk-free-rate model; bounded online portfolio estimators and detailed execution engines can produce controlled experiments.
limitation: No matched independent comparison here establishes real-market predictive edge or exact live fill fidelity. The choice and availability of benchmark/universe/input revisions remain part of the experimental contract.

finding: OptimizationAnalyzer computes the distribution of completed Sharpe ratios, parameter slices, clustering and modes from the supplied parameter grid; it also summarizes failed/zero-order cases available in that collection.
limitation: These are optional post-search diagnostics over retained parsed results. They are not independent ablations, complete failed-search coverage, dependence-adjusted uncertainty or a mandatory holdout gate.

scope: Native chronological dispatch and precomputed mode
finding: The event loop advances data and dispatches broker updates before ordinary strategy callbacks. The vectorized mode resets computed lines and advances only feeds with the earliest next timestamp before callbacks.
limitation: User code remains trusted: line indexing directly addresses the backing array at current index plus offset, so preloaded future values can be accessed deliberately. Cheat-on-open is an explicit alternate execution contract, not evidence that normal chronology fails.

finding: Cerebro runs supplied strategy classes over configured data feeds and enumerates parameter combinations.
limitation: A native supervised fit/evaluate owner was not located in this inspected surface. Strategy-level estimation needs an adapter that freezes training and evaluation data separately.

finding: The inspected engine/feed loop consumes market data and strategy callbacks; it does not own a supervised target stage.
limitation: Future label horizons and availability-time censoring become applicable to an added ML research adapter, not a fixed-signal execution test.

finding: optstrategy forms Cartesian parameter combinations over the configured feeds.
limitation: A purge/embargo/nested validation coordinator was not located in this API. Separate data feed date ranges can be caller-configured, but they are not automatic statistical isolation.

finding: Indicators may precompute over arrays while strategy callbacks advance one event at a time.
limitation: No fold-owned estimator preprocessing/OOF stacking protocol was located in this engine path. Mathematical causality of custom indicators and transform fit boundaries remain adapter obligations.

finding: The native optimization API enumerates strategy parameter sets and returns parameter/analyzer results.
limitation: A native calibrated-probability or nested threshold-selection owner was not located here. Compare this capability when a model adapter is supplied, not from analyzer headline metrics.

finding: TimeReturn can track portfolio NAV, fund value or a data price. Sharpe defaults to yearly periods, 1% annual risk-free rate, population standard deviation and no additional annualization; factors and sample correction are configurable.
limitation: These defaults differ materially from peers using daily sample volatility and zero risk-free rate. Return source, first-open rule, timeframe, annualization and fund treatment must be fixed explicitly in shared comparisons.

finding: Indicator test harnesses exercise preload/runonce/exactbars combinations against fixed expected values. The optimized-strategy test asserts expected cash/equity vectors across execution modes and parameter periods.
limitation: These tests were inspected, not executed in this academic audit. Their equivalence coverage is meaningful but does not prove all user strategies or independent fill-model realism.

finding: Cerebro parameter optimization schedules strategy simulations rather than a native supervised model-fitting loop.
limitation: Estimator convergence/warnings and conditioning must be evaluated in the model adapter. Indicator warmup and simulator completion are different properties.

finding: Cerebro retains all returned run results and invokes callbacks for finished candidates; optimized return objects carry parameters, analyzers and strategy class.
limitation: This is in-memory completed-result coverage, not a durable ledger of failed, interrupted, external or previous searches. A full search family requires caller-owned recording and common admission rules.

finding: The inspected optimization and Sharpe analyzer paths enumerate candidates and calculate marginal return moments.
limitation: No search-family DSR/PBO, dependence-aware uncertainty or automatic multiplicity gate was located in these surfaces. Native parameter sweep availability alone is not statistical evidence after selection.

finding: Native optimized results retain parameters and analyzers; TimeReturn emits dated period returns under explicit NAV/fund/data modes.
limitation: No canonical code/data-byte/environment equality gate was located in these paths. Shared comparison must align timeframe, capital flows, fund mode, execution mode and analyzer configuration.

finding: Native parameter enumeration runs configured feeds and returns their results.
limitation: No reserve/freeze/first-access final holdout mechanism was located in this API. That research capability needs a separate adapter; it is outside a raw execution-engine claim.

scope: Economic external validity and benchmark semantics
finding: A TimeReturn analyzer can observe an external data price as a benchmark, and executable regressions retain expected strategy cash/equity.
limitation: A price-return benchmark is not automatically cost/exposure matched. No matched held-out experiment here establishes predictive edge or market realism of a particular configured broker/fill path.

finding: Cartesian parameter sweeps and native test matrices across preload/runonce/exactbars support local sensitivity and implementation parity checks.
limitation: These are optional experiments. The inspected API does not require parameter stability, independently selected regimes, complete seeds or scientific ablations before results are reported.

scope: Native signal simulation and MA implementation
finding: Signal simulation passes the current row/column context and native entry/exit adapters select signals at that index. The inspected MA path uses rolling/exponential history.
limitation: The engine accepts batch arrays/custom functions and does not establish how input signals were produced. Predictor prefix invariance and execution lag belong to the signal contract; no general native causality proof follows from vectorization.

finding: Range/rolling/expanding splitters produce index sets, while the signal simulation consumes supplied arrays. No automatic estimator fit/evaluate owner was located in these inspected surfaces.
limitation: Split helpers alone do not keep feature fitting or tuning inside training. An ML adapter must enforce fit ownership; the fixed-signal execution track is not a model-training test.

finding: Fixed labels explicitly compute future relative returns using a backward shift; future mean labels reverse the series and use full-window rolling then shift.
limitation: These are intended target generators, not causal predictors. No availability-time metadata or automatic censoring at train/evaluation boundaries was located in these label/split helpers; create targets within the admitted horizon or purge externally.

finding: RollingSplitter builds moving windows, ExpandingSplitter anchors starts at zero, and range sets have configurable lengths with empty/oversized-set checks.
limitation: The inspected splitters cut by position, not event-end availability. They do not automatically purge label overlap, embargo folds or orchestrate nested fitting. Window overlap must not be counted as independent observations.

finding: The inspected indicator factory constructs parameter products and outputs; splitters expose indices rather than an estimator pipeline.
limitation: No managed fold-local fitted transform/OOF stacking contract was located here. Compare that capability through an explicit ML adapter, not raw simulation speed.

scope: Probability calibration and nested threshold selection
finding: The native signal adapter reads supplied entry/exit booleans; parameter combinations can be generated by the indicator factory.
limitation: Calibration and threshold-fit validation were not located in these execution/research primitives. A model adapter must supply their disjoint fit/evaluation protocol.

finding: Sharpe uses per-observation risk-free adjustment, nan-aware mean/std with configurable ddof and annualization from year frequency divided by data frequency. It returns NaN for fewer than two rows and infinity for zero standard deviation.
limitation: NaN support, risk-free units, frequency, period count and zero-variance behavior must be normalized across candidates. A native ratio with the same label need not equal another framework's ratio.

scope: Inspected numeric regression and formula tests
finding: Tests assert fixed Sharpe/rolling Sharpe results and DSR values, including an explicit moment-formula calculation over incomplete return arrays.
limitation: Tests were inspected, not executed in this academic audit. The DSR formula comparison reuses the same expected-maximum helper and does not independently validate statistical assumptions or all execution paths.

finding: Native parameter products and signal execution do not perform a managed statistical estimator fit in the inspected paths.
limitation: Model convergence/conditioning belongs to an added estimator adapter. Completion of a compiled array simulation is not evidence of model fit stability.

finding: Parameter products preserve parameter combinations and DSR can infer trial count from current columns or accept an explicit value.
limitation: Column count is not a complete search ledger: discarded, failed, manually tried or previous-run candidates are not recovered. The family and effective trial count remain caller responsibilities.

finding: DSR uses an expected-maximum Sharpe threshold based on trial count/variance and a skew/kurtosis-adjusted normal-CDF statistic. Annualized inputs are converted back to per-period values.
limitation: The helper is diagnostic, not automatic candidate admission. Default current-column count and variance do not establish the true search family/effective independent trials, and the inspected formula contains no serial-covariance correction.

scope: Indexed parameter arrays and saved objects
finding: Split arrays and parameter-labelled combinations retain local evaluation structure; pickle-based object persistence is available.
limitation: Object persistence does not establish canonical input-byte, source-revision, environment or benchmark-contract equivalence. Cross-run evidence acceptance needs an external manifest and common return/fill schema.

finding: Index splitters can create held-out ranges, but the inspected primitives do not own model selection or reserve final data access.
limitation: A held-out index set is not a frozen single-use holdout protocol. For platform comparison supply an adapter; for fixed-signal simulation this criterion is outside native scope.

finding: Native metrics and parameterized simulations can evaluate supplied paths and benchmark returns.
limitation: No matched cross-solution holdout experiment here establishes model edge or real fill validity. Signal production, universe/data revisions and execution assumptions remain material external inputs.

finding: Parameter Cartesian products, rolling/expanding windows and direct DSR arguments support repeatable sensitivity sweeps.
limitation: These are optional building blocks; the inspected code does not require ablations, seed sweeps, parameter plateau checks or independent regime replication before a result is accepted.

scope: Native TrailingStrategy percentage helper used from init
finding: The core run loop slices visible data/registered indicators through the current row. However, the shipped trailing helper backfills early ATR and fits the percentage-to-ATR multiplier on the full init sample. A recorded-fixture 192-versus-384-row probe changed the multiplier from 12.534609847694947 to 11.750024076167358 and changed all 153 fully observable historical stop distances; the fixed-six-ATR control changed zero.
limitation: Scope is TrailingStrategy.set_trailing_pct called in init with ATR40 and pct0.10, not every Backtest strategy. The probe reads native helper state through public Backtest.run; no orders or realized P&L were measured. Mature-row comparison excludes the 39 warmup rows; native ATR arrays themselves were equal across the common prefix.

finding: Backtest constructs a strategy for one supplied data frame; optimize repeatedly evaluates parameter combinations on that frame.
limitation: No managed estimator train/evaluation pipeline was located in the inspected API. Add an ML adapter with explicit fit ownership for platform comparison; one-frame strategy execution is outside that training contract.

finding: The run loop schedules strategy callbacks and processes supplied OHLC/trades without a native target-construction stage in the inspected core.
limitation: Label horizon, censoring and point-in-time supervision belong to a model adapter. The causal trailing-helper defect is separately captured under A01, not reclassified as label leakage.

finding: Native optimize shares the same supplied frame among candidate evaluations.
limitation: A purge/embargo/nested walk-forward coordinator was not located in the inspected run/optimize API. External slicing and an adapter can provide it; repeated optimization of one frame is not such a protocol.

finding: Strategy.init owns indicator preparation before the core exposes per-step prefixes.
limitation: There is no managed estimator transform/OOF-stack fit contract in this inspected path. Registered-indicator slicing does not retrospectively make full-sample fitted transformations causal.

finding: Optimize supports a named or callable objective and returns the best candidate on the evaluated data.
limitation: Probability calibration is outside this API. If a parameter represents a decision threshold, the reported best score is optimized in-sample performance; a separate nested validation/calibration adapter is required.

finding: Returns are resampled by inferred frequency; code chooses 252/365 or weekly/monthly/yearly annualization. Native Sharpe divides geometric annualized return by a compounded-volatility expression; buy-and-hold begins after the strategy indicator warmup.
limitation: Native Sharpe is not the arithmetic-mean/std convention used by several peers. Warmup-dependent benchmark start, final-trade policy and frequency inference can change comparison semantics; use common raw equity/trades for shared metrics.

scope: Inspected numeric regressions plus focused causal counterexample
finding: Tests assert a complete fixed historical strategy/statistics vector, trade ledger columns and boundary behavior. This assessment executed one focused recorded-data helper prefix counterexample with a mature-row control.
limitation: The inspected test suite was not executed by this academic audit; the focused probe establishes one local defect, not a global numeric failure rate. Regression snapshots are weaker than an independent execution/accounting oracle.

finding: Grid/SAMBO search evaluates backtest objectives; the core does not manage estimator likelihood convergence or fit-conditioning diagnostics.
limitation: Search-budget completion is not model convergence. Apply this criterion to an added fitted-model adapter, not to the execution loop.

finding: Grid optimization creates a parameter-indexed objective heatmap; SAMBO can return evaluated points/objectives and its raw result.
limitation: History return is optional, contains the selected objective rather than every full trial artifact, and does not include external or previous discarded searches. No complete failure/selection family ledger is established by the native return.

finding: The inspected optimize path selects the maximum objective over its evaluated grid/SAMBO points.
limitation: No DSR, PBO, dependence-aware uncertainty or familywise adjustment was located in this run/optimization/statistics surface. This is a bounded capability finding, not a claim that user strategies cannot supply such analysis.

finding: Run returns full equity/trade artifacts with dates; parameter heatmaps retain candidate coordinates.
limitation: No canonical input-byte/code/environment equality gate was located here. Indicator-dependent warmup changes the effective evaluation/benchmark start even when nominal input dates match, so common contracts must freeze burn-in and finalization.

finding: Native optimize reuses the supplied frame and reruns its best parameter set.
limitation: No separate reserved final-data access/freeze protocol was located in that API. A testing adapter must own final holdout admission and distinguish repeated validation from a first final evaluation.

scope: Economic external validity and baseline quality
finding: The statistics include a long-only buy-and-hold benchmark and the repository contains executable historical strategy regressions.
limitation: The buy-and-hold comparator is price-only and warmup-dependent; it is not automatically a cost/exposure-matched economic null. No matched independent study here establishes live fill realism or predictive edge.

scope: Parameter sweeps and random OHLC sensitivity
finding: Random-state-controlled grid sampling and a random_ohlc_data generator provide sensitivity primitives.
limitation: The generator calls DataFrame.sample with the same supplied random_state on every yield; a fixed integer replays that sample instead of advancing a local seeded stream. Its row/gap resampling also does not preserve general serial dependence. No mandatory ablation/independent-regime protocol is present in these helpers.

scope: Native equity/event Pipeline and bar callback chronology
finding: Equity pricing loader shifts daily OHLCV requests back one trading session and supplies adjustment-aware arrays. Event loaders admit next events only after knowledge timestamps and previous events after max(event date, knowledge time). Bar simulation processes existing orders before calling handle_data.
limitation: These are substantial native point-in-time primitives. Custom loaders/factors/external data remain trusted; supplied knowledge timestamps and corporate-action adjustments require validation. They do not prove all user predictors causal.

finding: CustomFactor consumes the next window for each date; native rolling regression fits each supplied historical window and exposes coefficient/statistic outputs.
limitation: This local estimation boundary is not a managed supervised train/validation/test pipeline. Factor parameters, feature fitting outside Pipeline and full strategy selection still need an explicit research adapter.

finding: Native event knowledge cutoffs and lagged pricing define observable predictor inputs, while rolling regressions fit supplied contemporaneous windows.
limitation: A future supervised label availability/censoring protocol was not located in these Pipeline/run surfaces. Event knowledge time is useful input infrastructure, not automatic label purging.

scope: Rolling factor window geometry versus research folds
finding: Native regression length must be at least2 and defines the input window; Pipeline can compute the same requested date range in chunks.
limitation: Rolling estimation and chunked execution do not create purged/nested independent evaluation folds. A model-selection adapter must own train/test geometry and outcome horizon exclusions.

scope: Window-local factor transforms and adjustment-aware data
finding: Pipeline formats each date's masked input window, and rolling regression derives its estimates from that window; pricing loaders attach dated corporate-action adjustments.
limitation: No general fold-fitted preprocessing/OOF stacking manager was located in these surfaces. Custom stateful factors must be checked for correct reset/reuse across chunks and independent evaluation.

finding: Pipeline returns factor values and statistical regression outputs for strategy callbacks.
limitation: A native supervised calibration/nested threshold-selection workflow was not located in this factor/runner surface. Add a model adapter for comparable decision-policy research.

scope: Native daily-return wrappers and delegated empyrical metrics
finding: ReturnsStatistic evaluates only daily returns through the current session and maps nonfinite scalars to None. Native metric registration delegates Sharpe/Sortino/drawdown to empyrical; period reports mask benchmark dates and convert NaN Sharpe to0.
limitation: Dependency formulas are bounded by empyrical-reloaded>=0.5.7 in this source audit, not an independently inspected exact dependency revision. Cumulative versus period missing-value conventions differ, so common raw return metrics should define them explicitly.

scope: Inspected point-in-time, adjustment and chunk tests
finding: Tests compare Pipeline output to expected asset/date values across chunk schedules, explicitly check event eligibility against knowledge/event dates, and compare adjustment-aware windows with separately constructed expected adjusted arrays.
limitation: Tests were inspected, not executed in this academic audit. They substantiate specific temporal/adjustment semantics but do not establish every data vendor/factor or independent fill-model validity.

finding: Native rolling linear regression delegates each supplied window to scipy.stats.linregress and exposes standard errors and related statistics.
limitation: No general fitted-model convergence/conditioning acceptance owner was located in the inspected Pipeline/runner surface. Closed-form regression output is not evidence of arbitrary model convergence.

finding: The native run utility executes one algorithm against a selected bundle and can serialize its performance frame.
limitation: A managed complete strategy/parameter search ledger was not located in these run/Pipeline surfaces. An external experiment adapter must retain failed, discarded and repeated attempts.

finding: RollingLinearRegression exposes slope/intercept/r-value/p-value/stderr from SciPy for each window.
limitation: These are marginal regression statistics, not post-strategy-selection inference. No overlapping-window/serial-dependence or multiple-family correction is applied in this factor, and native headline return metrics do not add such a protocol.

scope: Bundle vintage and dated performance outputs
finding: run_algo accepts a bundle timestamp; bundle loading selects an ingestion on or before that cutoff. Performance output can be serialized, and Pipeline loaders preserve calendar/adjustment semantics.
limitation: An ingestion timestamp is a useful reproducibility selector, not an immutable input-byte/source/environment manifest. Native default bundle time can float, and output pickle alone does not enforce experimental comparability.

finding: The native run utility accepts requested simulation dates and bundle vintage; Pipeline computes selected date ranges.
limitation: No model freeze/reservation/first-access final holdout mechanism was located in this surface. A separate research adapter must own final evaluation rather than relying on simulation dates alone.

finding: Native metrics compare algorithm and benchmark returns on matched report dates; pricing/event loaders support point-in-time input treatment.
limitation: No matched independent experiment here establishes predictive/economic edge or live-fill realism. Universe survivorship, data-vintage truth, benchmark support, costs and execution timing remain part of the research contract.

finding: Regression windows and Pipeline chunk sizes can vary, with native tests exercising randomized chunk schedules and corporate-action adjustment windows.
limitation: These are optional parameter/implementation checks. The inspected runner does not require model ablations, seed ensembles, parameter plateaus or independent regime replication before reporting a result.

finding: Backtesting shifts signal columns one bar; optional lookahead analysis recomputes truncated runs and compares aligned indicators and entry/exit outcomes. This is stronger native diagnostic coverage than merely accepting arbitrary batch predictors.
limitation: The diagnostic is not mandatory admission. It is limited by selected trades/cutoffs, minimum support and skipped forced exits; a clean report is not proof for every predictor/data regime. Full-frame feature callbacks remain trusted.

scope: FreqAI outer windows and base learned preprocessing
finding: For each backtest window, training data are cut before the outer cutoff; base regression/classifier pipelines split inner fit/evaluation data and fit transforms on inner train only.
limitation: Features are first populated on the complete supplied dataframe. Arbitrary feature/model callbacks can use broader information; inner shuffle/reversed order are configurable rather than universally forbidden.

scope: FreqAI target completion at outer cutoff and inner split
finding: Targets are regenerated on data ending strictly before outer training stop, then unavailable labels are dropped; an optional buffer trims both ends. This protects ordinary forward-shift targets against reading the next outer prediction period.
limitation: Targets are computed before the inner train/test split and no general inner horizon purge is present in that split call. Custom extrema/precomputed labels require an adequate buffer and explicit availability audit.

finding: A window generator validates positive integer training days, advances by configured backtest duration and places each outer prediction window immediately after its training period. Inner split defaults shuffle=False.
limitation: Window geometry is native to FreqAI, not a mandatory validation procedure for ordinary strategy hyperopt. Row/horizon overlap and irregular cadence still need the selected-target audit.

scope: FreqAI per-window learned feature and label pipelines
finding: Base regression training creates new feature/label pipelines, fits on inner training features/labels and transforms inner evaluation data. Optional PCA follows scaling in the pipeline.
limitation: Cached models/predictions and continual-learning configuration are different paths; raw feature causality is not repaired by fold-local scalers. Custom subclasses can replace the base pipeline.

scope: FreqAI model evaluation and strategy decision thresholds
finding: Native LightGBM receives inner evaluation data separately from fitted observations; example strategy applies explicit thresholds and requires do_predict==1 for entries.
limitation: No general independently assessed probability-calibration layer was located in these base/model paths. Strategy threshold choices and hyperopt selection require external untouched assessment; inner evaluation is not the final backtest sample.

scope: Trade-based versus balance-based Sharpe and return metrics
finding: Both trade-profit and daily-balance metric routes exist. Balance-based Sharpe uses daily last balances and percent changes; trade-based Sharpe divides total normalized profit by elapsed days but uses dispersion across trades.
limitation: These named Sharpe values are not interchangeable. Native annualization factor is365 and zero/NaN denominator can produce -100 as a selection sentinel; recompute a common equity-based metric before comparing frameworks.

scope: Lookahead regression tests and metric reference assertions
finding: Tests exercise explicitly biased/no-bias strategies and compare p-value/math behavior against expected/reference results. These are executable checks, including intentional negative controls.
limitation: Assertions were inspected in this comparative audit, not executed here. Formula checks do not establish global strategy causality or empirical probability calibration.

scope: Hyperopt stagnation and FreqAI model failures
finding: Hyperopt can stop on best-value stagnation. FreqAI catches a failed window fit, records metadata and emits null predictions instead of retaining a usable model for that window.
limitation: Stagnation and successful backend fitting are not general convergence/stability proofs. A benchmark must retain failed windows and inspect their effect on evaluation support.

finding: Completed epoch records retain loss, parameters, metrics, current index and best/random flags; results append one JSON line per evaluated epoch. Optuna receives evaluated losses.
limitation: The active study is created without durable storage in this constructor; only emitted records establish retained coverage. Unknown crashed/external searches and skipped duplicate candidates cannot become independent completed trials.

scope: Native trade p-value and hyperopt-selected utility
finding: Native p-value uses a one-sample t-test on normalized per-trade profit with fewer-than-two/constant-return fallbacks. Hyperopt minimizes a configurable same-backtest loss and applies a minimum-trade penalty.
limitation: No full-search multiplicity adjustment or serial-dependence correction is present in these computations. The per-strategy p-value is not a post-hyperopt false-positive guarantee.

scope: Strategy cache identity and FreqAI prediction reuse
finding: Backtest run ID hashes selected config, parameter-file state and strategy source bytes; reports retain evaluation dates. FreqAI reuses predictions using model path, row count/date-column presence and feature-list checks.
limitation: Run ID does not hash market-data bytes in this function. The inspected prediction gate does not compare actual timestamps/values. Immutable source identity and cross-run evaluation alignment need independent benchmark evidence.

scope: Final protected assessment beyond FreqAI windows/hyperopt
finding: Rolling prediction windows and separate model evaluation arrays are implemented; no reservation plus frozen-selection/exposure-attempt protocol was located in inspected backtest, hyperopt and FreqAI paths.
limitation: An ordinary historical timerange can be reused and optimized. A separate final holdout adapter/registry is required for untouched-assessment claims; this is not a defect in ordinary backtest execution.

scope: Executable strategy templates and quality comparison
finding: A concrete FreqAI template defines forward-return labels and entry/exit decisions, and configurable hyperopt losses produce measurable local objectives.
limitation: No same-budget external ranking or untouched cross-asset generalization was measured in this sub-audit. Templates are reproducible logic, not demonstrated economic baselines superior to another framework.

scope: Recursive sensitivity, feature pipelines and seeded search
finding: Native recursive analysis compares final indicator values across startup lengths and performs a truncated-input check. Hyperopt records/uses a sampler seed; optional PCA, outlier removal and noise expose explicit sensitivity choices.
limitation: Recursive diagnostics inspect selected pair/cutoffs and are not a full stability study. Sampler seed alone does not control all custom callbacks, backend randomness or source revisions.

scope: Native ts_init replay and callback/timer ordering
finding: Input can be sorted by initialization/availability timestamp; run requires sorted admission. Replay advances clocks before delivering each data item, processes exchange/data queues, and flushes timer/module events at timestamp boundaries.
limitation: These are concrete local chronology safeguards, not a proof of arbitrary strategy/indicator information sets. Correct ts_init meaning and complete same-timestamp streaming batches remain caller/data-contract obligations.

finding: The inspected backtest engine constructs and runs configured actors/strategies over admitted timestamped data.
limitation: A native supervised train/validation/test owner was not located in the engine/node/analysis surface. Model fitting requires an adapter; this is outside the fixed-signal event-replay contract.

finding: Native data replay respects supplied ts_init but does not construct future supervised targets in the inspected engine.
limitation: An ML adapter must translate event/label completion and local observation times into target availability rules. Generic event timestamps are not a target censoring protocol.

finding: Engine run accepts explicit start/end timestamps and node supports whole-run or streaming chunks.
limitation: Replay batching and run date ranges are execution geometry, not purged/nested model evaluation. A research adapter must own folds, horizon exclusion and family selection.

finding: Configured strategies receive timestamped events through the data engine; no fold-fitted preprocessing/stacking stage was located in this native surface.
limitation: Custom estimators may be embedded, but their fitted state and OOF construction require an explicit adapter audit.

finding: Native fill models expose execution probabilities with range validation and a seed.
limitation: These simulate order execution and are not supervised probability calibration or nested prediction-threshold selection. A learned decision policy needs its own adapter protocol.

finding: Sharpe compounds returns into UTC daily bins, uses sample standard deviation, default252 and NaN for insufficient/near-zero variance. The analyzer prefers resolvable daily portfolio-equity returns and otherwise can retain position-return statistics.
limitation: Primary return semantics can change with snapshot/currency/account support; position returns are not interchangeable with portfolio NAV returns. Daily equity calculation fills missing calendar days, so match calendar/return source and denominator explicitly rather than comparing labels alone.

scope: Inspected event-clock, numeric and canonical-output tests
finding: Tests assert same-timestamp timers observe all contemporaneous quotes, exact compounded daily-return examples, finite/undefined Sharpe cases and canonical-result divergence/encoding rejection.
limitation: Tests were inspected, not executed in this academic audit. Strong local invariants and serialization checks do not prove all strategy callbacks, fill models or live-market equivalence.

finding: Native engine run propagates callback/account/module errors, while probabilistic execution models sample configured distributions.
limitation: Runtime error propagation is distinct from model-fit convergence. An added estimator must supply conditioning, warning and fit-stability acceptance.

scope: Configured-run results versus complete search history
finding: BacktestResult stores run/config IDs, actual time bounds, iteration/event/order counts and return series; node returns a result for successful configured runs.
limitation: With raise_exception disabled, node logs an errored run and skips its result. This is not a durable complete attempted-search family ledger; strategy/model selection history remains external.

finding: The inspected analysis layer supplies marginal return/P&L ratios and optional benchmark-aligned metrics.
limitation: No native DSR/PBO, multiple-search-family correction or dependence-aware inferential acceptance protocol was located in the backtest/analysis surface. Seeded fill simulation is not such statistical control.

scope: Canonical result projection and run provenance
finding: The canonical-result type validates a versioned schema, normalization and exact bytes, and provides separate BLAKE3 digest and first-divergence methods. Ordinary results retain run/config/date/count information.
limitation: This is substantial native output comparability support. Equal result digests still do not establish identical source, input-market bytes, environments or statistically comparable evaluation protocols; those require an external contract manifest.

finding: Node executes configured replay ranges; engine can persist strategy state across managed lifecycle boundaries.
limitation: No reserve/freeze/first-access research holdout mechanism was located in the inspected backtest/node/analysis surface. State persistence alone is not a protected final statistical evaluation.

scope: Benchmark metrics and execution-model external validity
finding: Native benchmark alignment geometrically compounds daily returns and uses common timestamps; explicit seeded fill probabilities and execution models enable controlled scenarios.
limitation: No matched independent market study here validates predictive edge, probability calibration or fill realism. Benchmark timestamps/common support and execution assumptions must be predeclared.

scope: Seeded execution sensitivity and semantic result comparisons
finding: Fill model RNG can be deterministically seeded, run configs can vary assumptions, and canonical result digests/divergence checks support repeatable parity investigations.
limitation: These primitives do not force seed ensembles, calibrated model uncertainty, scientific ablations or independent regime tests before reporting a result.

scope: Native portfolio universe and estimation windows
finding: Backtest rejects non-monotone timestamps; the public universe property exposes data through target.now. Inverse-volatility/ERC/mean-variance estimators cut their input to now minus an explicit lag and lookback.
limitation: This establishes local information boundaries for the inspected built-ins. Strategy setup/additional data/custom algos remain trusted, and duplicate timestamps are accepted. Signal formation versus rebalance price timing still requires an explicit common contract.

finding: Built-in weight estimators use trailing returns through a configured lagged decision time rather than fitting one covariance over the entire backtest. Backtest deep-copies strategy templates.
limitation: This is online portfolio-estimation isolation, not a supervised train/validation/test research manager. Choices of lookback, covariance model and strategy family still need external validation.

finding: Native inverse-volatility/ERC/mean-variance algos fit return moments rather than future supervised labels.
limitation: Target horizon censoring is outside this portfolio-estimation contract. Apply it to an added predictive-model adapter; do not penalize the native engine for absent target construction.

finding: Inverse-volatility estimation supports trailing row counts or date offsets with lag; ERC and mean-variance use date-window lookbacks.
limitation: These rolling estimation windows are not a purged/nested out-of-sample experiment coordinator. When a learned forecast is introduced, its horizon/fit isolation must be supplied separately.

finding: Inverse-volatility recomputes sample volatility within the current lookback and drops invalid weights; ERC/mean-variance pass only trailing returns to covariance/optimization functions.
limitation: General feature preprocessing/OOF stacking is outside these algos. Covariance/solver implementation also depends on external ffn; this source audit establishes the passed data boundary, not all dependency internals.

finding: The inspected native portfolio algos return weights derived from historical return moments.
limitation: No calibrated prediction or nested classification-threshold selection protocol was located in these algos. That research feature requires an explicit model adapter.

scope: Native equity selection and delegated ffn statistics
finding: Backtest creates a virtual initial reference row, preserves strategy equity and computes metric input from one row before the first transaction. Native summary statistics delegate to ffn calc_perf_stats/GroupStats.
limitation: Metrics are dependency-bounded in this audit: bt declares ffn>=1.1.2, not an exact source revision. Trade-dependent starting dates can yield different sample lengths for nominally identical input periods; common metrics should use a frozen evaluation interval.

scope: Inspected chronology, accounting and baseline regression tests
finding: Tests assert non-monotone date rejection and explicitly solve a costed allocation equation independently before checking resulting position, fees and NAV in random-baseline execution.
limitation: These tests were inspected, not executed in this academic audit. They are valuable independent numeric examples but do not prove every strategy/solver/dependency path.

finding: ERC exposes maximum_iterations and tolerance and forwards them with covariance/risk-parity choices to ffn; mean-variance forwards weight bounds and risk-free rate.
limitation: The inspected bt wrapper drops NaN weights but does not inspect an explicit convergence report. Dependency solver acceptance and sensitivity remain outside the code boundary reviewed here.

scope: Returned collections of supplied backtests/random trials
finding: Result retains the supplied backtest list and name mapping; benchmark_random executes the requested simulations under copied assumptions and returns them for comparison.
limitation: This preserves locally supplied successful results, not a durable ledger of failed/interrupted or externally selected strategy families. Duplicate names and caller selection require independent provenance checks.

finding: RandomBenchmarkResult separates base and random statistics and plots their distribution against the base.
limitation: No multiplicity correction, DSR/PBO or dependence-adjusted hypothesis test was located in this benchmark/result surface. A histogram of an optional random family is not automatically valid post-selection inference.

scope: Matched random-baseline assumptions and native results
finding: benchmark_random preserves original capital, commission/cost model, integer-position policy, impact inputs and copied additional data; Result retains underlying backtests.
limitation: Useful local comparability does not establish source/data-byte/environment equality across independent runs. Native stats may start at different first-transaction dates, which the benchmark adapter must normalize.

finding: The native runner evaluates supplied data/strategy configurations and can compare many supplied or randomized backtests.
limitation: No reservation, model freeze or first-access holdout mechanism was located in this runner/result surface. Final research evaluation needs a separate adapter.

scope: Random portfolio baselines and economic generalization
finding: A native random-strategy benchmark reuses capital/cost/position assumptions and retains each baseline. This is a useful basis for matched portfolio nulls.
limitation: Null quality depends on the user-supplied random strategy and choices made before looking at outcomes. No independent matched study here establishes economic generalization or predictive edge.

finding: Random strategies, explicit lookback/lag/covariance settings and repeated backtests permit structured sensitivity experiments.
limitation: Random selection calls the global Python random generator and random weights delegate to ffn; the inspected benchmark entry point does not own a complete multi-library seed/ablation manifest. Reproducibility and independent regime selection remain caller-owned.

finding: A recorded-fixture public-getter probe queried before the first available quote and received the final future quote: bid/ask 45,056.0 at query 2024-01-01 14:29:59 UTC came from 2024-01-02 21:00 UTC. get_indexer(method=pad) returns -1, which the implementation passes to iloc.
limitation: Scope is the native CSV bid/ask getter before source history begins. No claim is made that every trading-session loop issues that query. The fixture retained original selected open/close values; the source itself synthesized daily quote times.

finding: Native fixed/single alpha signals and equal/fixed-weight portfolio optimizers expose callable execution interfaces.
limitation: A native supervised train/validation/test manager was not located in these alpha/portfolio/runner surfaces. A learned-model adapter must establish fit isolation.

finding: The inspected signal collection appends latest prices to bounded history and supplies technical signals, rather than constructing forward supervised targets.
limitation: Label horizon/censoring belongs to an added predictive-model workflow. Getter chronology is separately tested under A01.

finding: The runner supports start/end dates, burn-in and configurable rebalance dates.
limitation: Burn-in controls trading/performance recording, not train/test horizon overlap. A purged/nested research split coordinator was not located in this runner/portfolio surface.

finding: Signal buffers use bounded deques of observed prices; equal/fixed-weight optimizers do not fit supervised transforms.
limitation: No OOF stack or fold-owned learned preprocessing contract was located in this surface. An ML adapter must supply and verify it.

finding: Native single-signal alpha returns a configured scalar per current asset and equal-weight optimization maps it to weights.
limitation: No probability calibration or nested classification-threshold protocol was located in these built-ins. This is outside the fixed-allocation track.

finding: Sharpe uses zero-target arithmetic mean/population std with default252; Sortino divides by the standard deviation of negative returns. CAGR uses row count/periods and expects normalized cumulative equity.
limitation: These are not interchangeable with sample-std Sharpe, downside-RMS Sortino or elapsed-calendar CAGR. The drawdown routine seeds high-water marks at zero and starts at row1, omitting the first cumulative-equity value as a possible peak; initial declines can therefore be understated. This metric issue is source-inspected, not separately runtime-reproduced.

scope: Inspected accounting regressions and executed boundary probe
finding: Integration tests compare full portfolio history and approximate final holdings/P&L against stored expectations. A focused recorded-data probe reproduced the public prehistory getter defect.
limitation: The broader source suite was inspected, not executed in this academic audit. Golden histories do not independently validate all market assumptions, and the focused defect is not a global failure-rate estimate.

finding: The shipped equal/fixed-weight optimizers perform direct arithmetic/pass-through in the inspected portfolio surface.
limitation: Estimator solver convergence is not applicable to those direct algorithms. A different learned optimizer/model requires an adapter and its own convergence acceptance evidence.

finding: The native statistics writer emits one configured strategy/benchmark result and allocation history.
limitation: A managed hyperparameter/search-family trial ledger was not located in this runner/statistics surface. For a strategy-selection study, capture all attempts externally.

finding: Native summary functions calculate point estimates of return/risk statistics.
limitation: No managed strategy search or selection-adjusted/dependence-aware inference was located in these statistics/optimizer paths. This capability needs a research adapter.

scope: Native daily equity and JSON export
finding: The runner records daily closing equity after optional burn-in and exports strategy/benchmark IDs, curves and allocations.
limitation: The native equity accessor reduces timestamps to calendar dates; JSON conversion also reduces them to midnight and replaces NaN values with zero. This output is not a lossless intraday/provenance artifact and does not establish code/data/environment identity.

finding: The runner executes configured date ranges and rebalances; burn-in can suppress early trading and equity recording.
limitation: No model freeze, reservation or first-access final holdout protocol was located in this surface. Burn-in is not a protected statistical holdout.

scope: Portfolio baselines and economic external validity
finding: Equal/fixed-weight allocation and optional benchmark equity provide simple portfolio comparators, and end-to-end accounting regressions exist.
limitation: External predictive/economic validity is unmeasured. Daily simulated quote clocks, fees, exposure and the tested prehistory boundary must be considered before treating native benchmark results as a realistic market experiment.

finding: The runner supports buy-and-hold/daily/weekly/end-of-month rebalance policies, optional burn-in and signal history lengths.
limitation: These knobs enable manually coordinated sensitivity studies; no required ablation, seeded search manifest or independent-regime replication was located in this surface.

scope: Separate local/exchange event and response timelines
finding: The replay scheduler distinguishes local data, exchange data and local/exchange order events, advances the appropriate processor and stops at the requested timestamp. Order/feed waits expose events when their simulated local response time is reached.
limitation: This is meaningful native information-set modeling for order-book replay, conditional on valid event timestamps and chosen latency models. It does not prove arbitrary strategy features causal or validate recorded latency calibration; it is outside an OHLC-bar equivalence track.

finding: The native replay scheduler evolves exchange/local/order state rather than owning a supervised estimator workflow.
limitation: Train/evaluation isolation requires a research adapter. Missing ML fitting is outside the native order-book execution contract, not a low robustness score.

finding: Native local/exchange processors consume timestamped market/order events.
limitation: No target horizon/censoring contract was located in this replay surface. A prediction adapter must define label availability using local observation times and exchange/response latency.

finding: The example parameter grid evaluates specified date ranges; statistics helpers can partition output by calendar period.
limitation: Calendar report partitions and repeated replay dates are not a managed purged/nested validation coordinator. A model/search adapter must own independent temporal assessment.

finding: The native engine accepts model implementations and replays state/events without a fold-owned feature fitting phase.
limitation: OOF stacking and transform fit locality were not located in this execution surface. They become applicable when an estimator adapter is supplied.

finding: Queue and latency models parameterize execution behavior; the example search varies strategy spread/grid settings.
limitation: Execution probability/latency assumptions are not a supervised probability-calibration protocol. Calibrated predictors and nested trading-threshold fitting require a separate research adapter.

scope: Native mark-to-market P&L and annualized metrics
finding: Recorder stores timestamp, midpoint, balance, position, fees and trade activity. Native Sharpe/Sortino use increments of net equity, annualized by samples/day times configurable252 trading days.
limitation: These are P&L-increment ratios, not automatically capital-normalized percentage-return metrics. Sampling frequency is inferred from the first interval; inconsistent intervals only warn. Freeze book size, currency, resampling and annualization before cross-engine comparison.

scope: Inspected event-clock and queue model tests
finding: Native tests assert that local/exchange processors skip events not visible to them and that current replay timestamps advance as expected. L3 queue tests assert specific fill/removal outcomes.
limitation: Tests were inspected, not executed in this academic audit. These local state invariants do not validate a complete live-exchange fill oracle, latency fit or counterfactual impact model.

finding: The inspected latency model returns configured values and the replay loop evolves deterministic model state.
limitation: Model-estimation convergence is outside this native executor contract. Calibrating latency/queue parameters or adding learned forecasts requires an explicit fitting/evaluation adapter.

finding: The executable grid-search example enumerates parameter combinations and embeds spread/grid/skew settings in output names while reporting subprocess return codes.
limitation: This is an example-level record convention, not a durable complete trial/failure/selection ledger. Full external searches and parameter families are caller-owned.

finding: The inspected metric code calculates marginal P&L ratios and the example executes a parameter grid.
limitation: No DSR/PBO, multiple-family adjustment or dependence-aware inferential acceptance gate was located in these native stats/example-search surfaces. Different replay assumptions cannot be treated as independent candidate draws automatically.

scope: Replay state records and execution assumptions
finding: Native per-asset records retain balance/position/fees/activity over time; the example command passes data/latency file paths, tick/lot sizes and strategy parameters explicitly.
limitation: These records do not constitute a canonical source/input-byte/environment equality manifest. Record sampling, fee/queue/latency model, event ordering and market-data provenance must be fixed for a fair specialist comparison.

finding: Native replay and its example grid use supplied date/file ranges.
limitation: No reserve/freeze/first-access final holdout mechanism was located here. A research adapter must own model selection and final-data access; this is outside the order-book replay primitive.

finding: Native code distinguishes maker/taker fills, partial remaining quantity, local/exchange latency and queue assumptions, giving the specialist track substantially richer modeled execution than OHLC-only replay.
limitation: Model detail is not validation against actual executions. The inspected fill routine updates simulated order/account state, while market observations remain a replay; real counterfactual market response and calibrated queue/latency accuracy are unmeasured here. Do not synthesize a book from OHLC and claim an equivalent benchmark.

finding: Generic latency/queue implementations and the executable parameter grid allow separate studies of strategy and execution assumptions.
limitation: No mandatory latency/queue calibration, sensitivity envelope or independent-regime replication is enforced by these building blocks. Runtime comparisons must stay within a matched order-book track.

scope: Alpha158 feature expressions and native signal strategies
finding: Expression engine explicitly supports positive and negative Ref offsets. Native TopkDropout and WeightStrategy query the previous trade-calendar step for their prediction signal. This is real execution-lag control.
limitation: Arbitrary expressions/signals are trusted; a negative Ref in a predictor can consume future data. No universal prefix-invariance enforcement is present in these paths.

finding: LGBModel obtains only named train/valid segments for fitting and uses the infer feature view for test prediction. Built-in learned normalizers restrict fit observations to explicitly supplied dates.
limitation: DataHandler prepares whole requested data before segment fetch; arbitrary processors receive full frames, and fit bounds are supplied separately from dataset segments. Matching bounds and callback information use remain caller obligations.

scope: Alpha158 forward labels and configured static versus rolling workflows
finding: Alpha158 label is Ref(close,-2)/Ref(close,-1)-1. Raw labels are prepared for the handler range, then DatasetH selects date segments; the shipped static LightGBM YAML has contiguous train/valid/test periods. Rolling wrapper explicitly truncates non-test support by horizon+1.
limitation: Static segment slicing does not itself censor labels at each segment end; boundary-label completion can cross into the next segment. This is inspected control flow, not an executed leakage-rate estimate. Properly configured truncation is a distinct protected path.

scope: RollingGen and MultiHorizonGen temporal task construction
finding: Expanding/sliding generators shift named segments and deepcopy task configurations. Configured trunc_days removes non-test support near test start; MultiHorizonGen uses horizon+label_leak_n.
limitation: Direct RollingGen defaults trunc_days to None. The helper is not automatically applied to all DatasetH tasks, and dates alone do not prove target availability.

finding: Normalizers fit inside explicit date bounds; processor fit/transform pipelines and task deep copies are implemented.
limitation: Rolling handler modification extends its load end date; it does not universally derive new processor fit bounds from every training segment. Rolling also supports a shared cached handler. Independent fold-local fitting must be checked for the selected configuration.

scope: LGBModel validation selection and native signal analysis
finding: Training can use validation observations for LightGBM early stopping, and test prediction is a separate operation. Native signal records preserve predictions and test labels.
limitation: A general probability-calibration/threshold-fitting pipeline with independent calibration assessment was not located in these inspected model/record paths. Regression rank signals are not implicitly calibrated probabilities.

finding: Risk analysis supports sum and product accumulation; default sum annualizes arithmetic mean and computes drawdown on cumulative summed returns. Native portfolio records analyze excess returns with and without cost.
limitation: Default daily scaler is238, not a universal252/365 convention. Product mode uses geometric per-period mean with log-return standard deviation. Match accumulation, baseline, cost and annualization before comparing metric names.

scope: Processor, temporal sampler and order-fill assertions
finding: Tests contain alternate normalization calculations, temporal-sampler alignment assertions and explicit fill-ratio expectations.
limitation: These assertions were inspected, not executed in this comparative sub-audit. No universal independent numerical oracle or empirical calibration result follows from their presence.

scope: LGBModel optimization history and failure semantics
finding: LightGBM early stopping and per-iteration train/validation metric logging are implemented. Fit raises on missing/empty/multilabel data outside its supported contract.
limitation: Stopping on validation is model selection, not proof of numerical convergence or seed stability. Backend optimization mathematics remain delegated; no package-wide convergence admission policy was established.

scope: MLflow recorder and rolling experiment inventory
finding: Recorder has running/finished/failed states, run IDs, parameters, artifacts and end-run status. Rolling orchestrates a supplied task list.
limitation: This is retained experiment history, not a complete global search ledger. Rolling can delete the previous named experiment before retraining; externally attempted or selectively supplied searches remain unknown.

scope: Selection-adjusted inference in inspected evaluation and record paths
finding: Inspected risk and portfolio analysis calculate return/volatility, information ratio, drawdown and benchmark-relative statistics. No DSR/PBO or full-family adaptive-selection adjustment was located in these paths or the bounded package search.
limitation: Not located is not a proof of repository-wide absence. Reported performance and IC diagnostics do not alone establish dependence-aware inferential validity.

scope: Experiment provenance and emitted prediction/portfolio artifacts
finding: MLflow recorder logs invocation, selected environment variables and Git working-state outputs; signal/portfolio records retain indexed predictions, labels, returns and positions. A focused native AsyncCaller probe also reproduced that a worker callback exception can let wait return normally while later queued work never runs.
limitation: No Limen-style exact cross-family sample/execution compatibility admission was established in these record paths. Immutable input bytes and model/dependency identities must be supplied by the benchmark adapter. Only AsyncCaller was executed in that probe; implications for MLflowRecorder completion/artifact persistence follow from inspected decorator/wait wiring, not an executed recorder failure.

scope: Protected final-holdout admission versus named test segment
finding: LGBModel predicts a named test segment and SignalRecord saves test labels; recorder allocates an ordinary experiment run. No protected data reservation, frozen-selection-before-access gate or exposure-attempt ledger was located in these paths.
limitation: Named test data and experiment tracking are useful but do not by themselves protect an untouched final assessment. A separate benchmark-owned holdout protocol is required for that claim.

scope: Executable Alpha158 LightGBM strategy and benchmark configuration
finding: A concrete LightGBM/Alpha158 workflow supplies dates, market, benchmark, top-k strategy, account and transaction costs, enabling reproducible candidate specification.
limitation: No equal-budget cross-solution or untouched cross-market quality experiment was executed here. Executable benchmark configuration and recorded examples do not establish an edge.

finding: Task generators parameterize horizons and rolling windows; recorder saves parameters, working-tree evidence and serialized artifacts.
limitation: These mechanisms do not prove stable outcomes across costs, seeds, dates or features. Optional cached handlers, backend seeds and provider data must be frozen to reconstruct the same experiment.

scope: Timestamp replay and shipped indicator recurrences
finding: Timestamp replay applies the current event before executing only routes updated by it. The inspected Rust SMA and EMA bodies consume backward windows/recurrences.
limitation: This scopes native event delivery and two indicator implementations; it does not prove arbitrary strategy callbacks or every indicator causal. Native Python wrappers depend on jesse-rust; matching source version is pinned separately, but wheel/source binary identity was not established.

finding: Fitness runs separate training and testing backtests; the returned optimization score is computed from training metrics only.
limitation: Caller-supplied dates/candle dictionaries determine separation; the inspected date loader does not establish that the two windows are disjoint. Testing metrics are exposed for each eligible candidate, allowing human selection on them.

finding: Rule significance aligns signal at t with log return from close t to close t+1 and drops the final signal without a next return.
limitation: This validates the response alignment in this diagnostic only. Native general ML target censoring/availability contracts were not located in the inspected strategy optimization path; an ML adapter must supply them.

finding: Training and testing periods have explicit separate start/end dates and their own warmup candles.
limitation: No purge, embargo, nested fold generator or automatic overlap rejection was located in the inspected optimization date loader/research API. Reusing a testing window across trials does not create independent final evidence.

finding: The native optimization path passes strategy hyperparameters and separately supplied candle sets into isolated backtests; it does not supply a general fold-fitted feature/stacking pipeline in the inspected surface.
limitation: For the execution track this is outside the native contract. Compare preprocessing leakage only after an ML adapter defines fit and transform ownership.

scope: Strategy parameter selection; no probability calibration contract
finding: The native optimizer selects on a training objective while separately calculating testing metrics for eligible candidates.
limitation: Testing outcomes remain visible during search. Probability calibration, threshold nesting and a final untouched calibration assessment were not located in this optimization path.

finding: Sharpe uses sample standard deviation and an explicit default 365 observations/year; smart Sharpe applies a lag-one autocorrelation-derived penalty. CAGR/Calmar are withheld when timestamps are unavailable. The significance diagnostic reports detrended signed next-bar returns.
limitation: The significance response is not realized net strategy P&L. Observation annualization, timestamp support, undefined metrics and the assumed autocorrelation model must be aligned before comparing native headline ratios.

scope: Inspected numerical, alignment and isolation tests
finding: Indicator tests assert fixed expected values and sequential/scalar agreement; rule-significance tests assert next-bar alignment, seeded batch-count invariance and runtime cleanup. Public Rust indicator source is available at a separately pinned revision.
limitation: Tests were inspected, not executed for this assessment. Same-code scalar/vector agreement is not an independent financial oracle; matching Rust dependency version alone does not prove installed binary identity.

finding: The inspected native search evaluates strategy hyperparameters through backtests, not a managed statistical estimator fit loop.
limitation: Model convergence, conditioning, calibration stability and fit-warning acceptance become applicable when an ML adapter is added. Optimizer budget completion should not be called model convergence.

scope: Dashboard Optuna history versus research API
finding: Dashboard optimization creates/resumes a SQLite-backed Optuna study and stores parameters, score and training/testing metrics for returned trials.
limitation: The research API keeps only ranked best candidates in its return. Fitness catches general failures and returns a low-score/empty-metric result, so a completed trial is not necessarily a successful experiment; complete external search history is not enforced.

finding: Optional rule significance zero-centers signed detrended next-bar returns and samples geometrically sized contiguous blocks with circular wraparound. Seeded output is independent of batching; the reported p-value is the fraction of simulated means at least the observed mean.
limitation: This handles a chosen local dependence model, not a searched family. No multiple-rule/parameter-selection correction is applied in this entry point. Finite Monte Carlo estimates can be zero because the implementation uses the raw exceedance fraction.

finding: Optimization forwards balance, fee, simulation model, annualization, leverage and warmup explicitly into isolated worker backtests and attaches train/test metrics to saved trials.
limitation: This improves assumption traceability but no exact input-byte/code/environment acceptance manifest or cross-run comparability gate was located in these paths. Different windows or simulation assumptions must remain separate cohorts.

finding: A testing backtest uses the same candidate parameters after training evaluation, and its metrics do not enter the computed score.
limitation: Testing metrics are published for many candidates; the path does not implement a reserved single-use final holdout or a freeze-before-access gate. Treat this as repeated validation, not protected final evidence.

finding: Native rule-significance and Monte Carlo paths can evaluate a supplied strategy under explicit assumptions; tests include noise/signal examples.
limitation: No matched cross-solution experiment here establishes real-market predictive edge, economic generalization or fidelity of assumed fills. A diagnostic on a selected strategy is not independent holdout evidence.

scope: Seeded dependence and candle perturbation sensitivity
finding: Stationary-bootstrap block length and seed are exposed. A moving-block candle pipeline resamples contiguous multivariate blocks using an explicit RNG; Monte Carlo supports alternative candle perturbation models.
limitation: These are optional robustness experiments with assumed perturbation distributions. Their existence does not show a strategy passed sensitivity analysis, and independently sourced market regimes remain necessary.
